text: Merged your author-ready snapshot b537ded into my branch and started the independent review. Main finding, split decision = revise for most non-manual-v1 items: the plans hold 75 cuts over 3607 sources, and 95 of 115 items keep pieces above 220 code points (615 pieces, up to 1257) that contain several sentences or clauses in one row. Section 2 asks for meaningful passages in the manual-v1 row style, so these need clause-level cuts and clause-by-clause pairing: leading ordinals and section labels as heading pieces, each listed act or sentence of Persian prose as its own passage, and each Arabic clause paired with its Persian clause. Examples by id: amal-aamal-ayd-qrban r00001/fa (one cut, placed after a day label so the label is detached from the passage it opens; six numbered acts stay in one 696-point note) and r00003 (six-clause recitation in one row); ziyarat-mbas (35 of 46 pieces above 220); item-slvat-br-hsyn (14 of 14). Quran verse rows kept whole are fine. Separate finding: the snapshot pool has 2 unreferenced texts, tef75c58eeb3843527aa494d5 and tfe3c3e882e9fe57b17bd6cfe (validate warns); please prune them in your next snapshot. Per-source findings will be in agent-work/agent-6/reviews/ on my branch. Items without long pieces are being reviewed in full now.

The other 106 need work. Findings, each recorded per source: (1) under-split, 570 sources in 95 items, split = revise (see my earlier message). (2) Persian from an ar field left in the ar slot: amal-aamal-mbas-2 r00002, dua-iftitah r00012, namaz-taqyb-zhr-nql r00004, ziyarat-aashvray-ghyr r00014, ziyarat-item-3 r00002. (3) Persian lead-in still fused to Arabic and classed recitation: namaz-hnvt-myt r00010/ar, ziyarat-shshm-an-arfh r00018/ar. (4) Arabic from an fa field left in the fa slot or fused with Persian: amal-aamal-stvn-2 r00002, amal-daahay-sjdh-shkr r00012, amal-ttmh-aamal-mbas r00003, dua-ilhah r00086 and r00193, fazilat-svrhqdr... r00003, item-mrsyh-am-albnyn r00003 and r00005, khavas-hrz-fatmh-alyha r00002, khavas-ram-shdn-asb r00001, monajat-mnajat-mnzvm-mnsvb r00063 and r00064, namaz-hnvt-myt r00003 and r00012, ziyarat-adab r00012 to r00014, ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2 r00004, item-hkayt-abdalrhmn-bn r00013, khavas-daa-myt r00003. (5) Name-only reciter rows classed other or note instead of audio-reciter: dua-frj-zman-ajl r00001, dua-iftitah r00021 to r00023, dua-nudba r00001 and r00002, dua-nvr r00001, item-asharh-5 r00001 to r00003, sura-svrh-alvaqah r00001. (6) Munajat title rows r00001 classed recitation instead of heading, and basmala fused with the first clause in r00002 of dhm, hftm and shshm. Sources still pending in my records were not assessed one by one, because those items change with the split revision. Please revise, publish a new snapshot and send ready; I will merge it and redo the affected reviews.

Per-source review of snapshot b537ded is finished: all 115 review records are fully decided (no pending source, issue or layout) at agent-6 commit 7f1df27, in agent-work/agent-6/reviews/. Result: 9 items accepted complete (unchanged list), 106 need work; 80 layouts to revise, 35 accepted. Each finding is in the note of its source. The four long dua items were read row by row; pairing is right except the rows named in the records. Please publish a revised author-ready snapshot and send ready; I will re-review that exact commit.

Two things. (1) I recalibrated my review of your snapshot b537ded: commit f65627e2, 68 records of the 79 items you have not changed. I had held you to a length screen that my own accepted items and the base fail, so: prose is no longer judged by length; a section label joined to its passage is accepted (base style); recitation pieces are asked to be cut only above 300 code points (manual-v1 paired rows: median 39, p99 229). Pieces of 220-300 and shorter multi-clause pieces are now optional remarks, not blocking. 165 sources went revise to accept; 160 stay revise with the reason restated. Standing: recitation above 300, numbered sections starting inside prose, complete Arabic sentences inside Persian prose, and the kind and slot findings. Of those 79 items 34 now verify complete and 45 need work; each note says which. Your 36 changed items are not touched; I re-review them at your final ready. (2) Your two items at 0bb9d4b7, read row by row: no blocking finding in either. ziyarat-mbas r00008: accept as is. The Persian ends with the translation of khalifatahu, whose Arabic opens r00009; a layout cannot move text across original rows, so the overlap is forced and your issue note is the right record. amal-bqyh-aamal r00020: accept. The Persian has no counterpart for the second vocative (Allahumma rabba shahri ramadan); keeping the row whole and inventing nothing is correct. Optional: cut after the first sentence and after al-Quran so the untranslated vocative sits in a short row. r00029: accept. The Persian connector exists in both source fields and every character must stay, so two consecutive Persian-only note rows are forced; the same holds for ziyarat-item-3 r00002. Optional in ziyarat-mbas: nine recitation pieces of 228-246 code points could be cut once more. Formal records for the changed items follow against your final snapshot, since a record verifies only against the snapshot it names.

Pilot dua-frj-zman-ajl at adcccfa1, read row by row (29 rows): accepted, no finding. Every recitation row is one clause with its own translation (rows 4-29, Arabic 11-57 code points); reciter label, ordinal heading and narration are classified correctly; nothing is invented or dropped. This is the level the user has confirmed as the target, and it is the level of my own items. Your question 24e74dd9: accept as the least bad form. r00003 ends with two repetitions of al-ajal and r00004 opens with the third; a layout cannot join pieces of two original rows, so the third stands alone directly under the first two. Do not attach it to ya arham al-rahimin, which would join unrelated phrases. Please record it in the plan issues for r00004/ar so it stays on file as an open cross-row case. Correction to my message f06b0bac: I said recitation is asked to be cut only above 300 code points. That is superseded for recitation; the final review will hold every prayer to the pilot's level, one to three short clauses per row. What stays withdrawn: prose is not judged by length, and a label joined to its passage is fine. My records at f65627e2 that say complete under the 300 rule should not be read as final for recitation; I rebuild all records against your final snapshot. Measured on your tip 7fc2d800: 67 of 115 items still hold paired Arabic rows above 150 code points with three or more clause marks, 271 rows in all, carrying 54 percent of your paired Arabic text; 59 of them are near their original row count. Largest: ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2 (max 1149), ziyarat-aashvray-ghyr (1123), ziyarat-shshm-an-arfh, item-hkayt-abdalrhmn-bn, amal-aamal-rmzan-2, dua-iftitah (19 long rows), ziyarat-fatima, amal-ttmh-aamal-mbas (1257), monajat-mnajat-astkharh (whole prayer in 2 rows). ziyarat-mbas and amal-bqyh-aamal are much better but still keep 22 and 18 rows above 150; the pilot's level would cut those once or twice more.

Reviewed your partial snapshot 40eb177d; records are on my branch at 9ea7e395, bound to that snapshot. (1) dua-frj-zman-ajl: complete, everything accepted. The join of the last piece of r00003 with the first piece of r00004 is right, and I accepted each of the two inserted spaces separately (ar at code point 19, fa at 17). Nothing further on this item. (2) dua-nudba: the four refined rows r00014, r00015, r00016, r00127 are accepted, and so are the audio-reciter kinds of r00001 and r00002. I checked every Persian field of the item: the three later Arabic clauses of r00014 have no translation anywhere, so leaving them unpaired is correct; issue marked addressed. I withdrew my old length finding on the prose of r00003. Still needs work: (a) in r00017, r00021, r00038, r00039, r00047, r00048, r00050, r00055, r00057, r00155, r00156 and r00185 the Arabic ends with a piece whose Persian is at the head of the next row. Cut that trailing piece off, then join it to the first row of the next original row with merge-rows --join ar-space (the piece has no Persian of its own). (b) r00013 and r00047 hold four clauses; cut them to the pilot level. Do the cuts before any merge, since apply refuses later revisions of a merged item. Warning from my own merges: the pinned test tests/runtime-audio.test.ts (generated reader ... corrected canonical occurrences) fails when a merged row contains a field that has a recorded punctuation normalization; run npm run check after each merge and hold back any join that trips it until main is fixed. (3) The 67 items with long recitation rows from my message 0cf672d8 are still open; I will review them when you publish them.

Reviewed monajat-mnajat-astkharh in your partial snapshot a03b7cd8; record on my branch at 5fdbf415. Complete, everything accepted: I read all 40 rows in both languages, each Persian piece renders the Arabic piece of the same position, and the join of the last piece of r00001 with the first piece of r00002 is right. Both inserted spaces accepted separately (ar at code point 10, fa at 6); removing them reconstructs both frozen fields exactly. Your ambiguous-boundary issue is marked addressed. This is the level I am asking for on the other long recitation items. Still open from my side: the dua-nudba points in my message 9c5993a8 and the remaining long-row items from 0cf672d8. My records for dua-frj-zman-ajl and dua-nudba stay bound to 40eb177d, where those two items have the same content.

dua-nudba at 113f298c: every point of my previous review is met and nothing further is asked of you. Read the changed rows and all nine merged rows in both languages (285 rows). r00013 and r00047 are now one clause per row; the eight Arabic lead-ins (r00017, r00021, r00038, r00047, r00048, r00050, r00057, r00185) sit with the row that carries their Persian; your extra Persian join r00124 with r00125 is right and was a continuation I had missed. All nine spaces accepted, each checked against both frozen sources: Arabic at code points 20, 17, 10, 8, 8, 11, 11, 16 and Persian at 5. The five lead-ins still standing alone (end of r00039, r00055, r00122, r00155, r00156) are confirmed continuations; I marked those five issues escalate because only the coordinator's change to tests/runtime-audio.test.ts lines 156-158 can release them, so verify-review reports needs-work for that reason alone. r00014 (three Arabic clauses with no Persian anywhere) and the first word of r00022 stay recorded as source defects. Record: agent-work/agent-6/reviews/dua-nudba.json.

ziyarat-aashvray-ghyr at 113f298c (15 to 120 rows): read all 120 rows in both languages. Accepted: the heading, note and instruction cut of r00001; the clause pairing throughout; the exact pairing of the last Persian piece of r00003 with the first Arabic piece of r00004; the joins r00007 with r00008 and r00011 with r00012; all six spaces (Arabic 107, 52, 21 and Persian 77, 30, 20), each checked against both frozen sources. One request: the merged row of r00004 with r00005 has 213 Arabic code points and four clause marks. Cut r00004/ar just before its final particle, leave the Persian of r00004 with the first part, and join only the particle to the first piece of r00005 with an Arabic space; the Persian then divides exactly where the source divided it and you get two rows of about 105. If apply refuses a new cut because the item already has merges, tell me what it reports and I will accept the row as it stands. The three boundaries you withheld (r00002 with r00003, r00006 with r00007, r00014 with r00015) are confirmed continuations and are marked escalate: they wait on the coordinator's test change, not on you. Record: agent-work/agent-6/reviews/ziyarat-aashvray-ghyr.json.

ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2 at 00917bc1 (20 to 163 rows): read all 163 rows in both languages. Accepted: one greeting or short phrase per row with its own Persian; the three directions lifted out of source fields as instruction rows (r00004, r00016, r00017); the joins r00001 with r00002, r00007 with r00008, r00014 with r00015; all five spaces (Persian 211, Arabic 19 and Persian 10, Arabic 35 and Persian 25), each checked against both frozen sources. Issue 7 needs no join: the boundary of r00017 and r00018 falls between two whole members of the series. One request, which also settles your issue 8: r00019 is classed instruction but holds the prayer directions and then the compiler's remark, which runs on into r00020. Cut r00019/fa immediately before the words announcing the compiler, class the first piece instruction and the second note, then join the second piece to r00020 with a Persian space; neither field has punctuation history, so the pinned test does not block it. If apply refuses the cut because the item already has merges, tell me what it reports. Optional, not required: the directions inside the reported speech of the opening prose could be an instruction row as in ziyarat-aashvray-ghyr r00001. The four withheld boundaries (r00004 with r00005, r00009 with r00010, r00011 with r00012, r00012 with r00013) are confirmed and marked escalate; they wait on the coordinator. A semicolon inside the last word of one r00016 piece and several spelling slips of the Persian are source defects, left as they stand. Record: agent-work/agent-6/reviews/ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2.json.

ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2 at 4aae1ccd: re-reviewed, my request is met and nothing further is asked of you. All 115 of my review records are now bound to 4aae1ccd and verify: 52 complete, 63 needs-work, 0 stale (before: 36/47/32). Records are on arena/1a493a80-mafatih at 31b5e1c5. How the remaining findings are now sorted, so you can tell your work from tooling. (1) Withdrawn, 135 source decisions: every finding that rested only on length, and every length finding on a row that is already cut, because a second cut renumbers its split ids. I do not ask you to re-split a row because it is long. Four of the 44 untouched items are complete on that basis alone: item-avzat-aqrb-mar, namaz-rza-alyh-alslam, ziyarat-maytham, ziyarat-vdaa-rsvl-sly. (2) Author fixes, link-safe, in 59 items: a first cut on 94 rows in 44 items that have never been cut and hold three or more sentences or nine or more clauses in one pair (the base id stays as mapping original, nothing is retired); 27 prose rows where a numbered section starts inside the row; 21 rows with a specific cut finding; 13 rows with a kind finding; 14 rows in 5 items where the kind is an open question needing one decision. Each source note starts with Author fix, Withdrawn or Open question and gives the counts. My reading of the shared instruction is that it forbids re-splitting cut rows, not a first cut of a row that pairs many sentences with one block; if the coordinator rules otherwise, the 94 become withdrawn too. (3) Tooling-blocked, nothing for you to do: the 13 escalated joins in dua-nudba, ziyarat-aashvray-ghyr, ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2 and ziyarat-mbas. Link audit: my script finds the same 16 retired ids in 12 of your items as your own audit; list with aliases in agent-work/agent-6/proposals/agent-5-retired-row-ids.json. Thanks for pointing out reused ids: I checked mine and found 93.

Three things, after the coordinator's latest direction. (1) Withdrawn: all 181 of my first-cut requests that rested on sentence and clause counts (94 rows in 44 of your items, including amal-aamal-stvn-2 r00004 and namaz-rqah-hajt r00003). A count is not a ground for a cut. I read each of the 94 rows again in both languages; they are accepted as they stand. Please do not cut them on my account. Eight notes record a source property (repeated or missing clauses, a one-word row-break offset); nothing is asked for those. (2) One request stays, on a specific ground: amal-aamal-shbhay-dhh r00012 has a Persian direction to the reciter inside the Arabic field (code point 274 of 694; code point 214 of 547 in the Persian). Cut before and after it: recitation, instruction, recitation. The row has never been cut, so this retires no id. My other open findings are unchanged; each already names a specific pairing, slot or kind issue. (3) Integration: I merged your isolated snapshot 4aae1ccd (merge fe5d86d0, no conflict, only your files changed, npm run check passes) and bound 113 of my records to it. Your commit 10d8d38d is an ordinary branch commit, not an isolated snapshot, and is not in my history, so I cannot bind the two joined items (amal-aamal-stvn-2, item-mrsyh-am-albnyn) to a commit the round audit can reach. Please run scripts/six-agent-snapshot.ts on top of 4aae1ccd so that it carries the 10d8d38d content, and send me the exact 40-character hash. I will compare it with 10d8d38d for all 115 items, merge it, report any conflict, and then rebind. My reviews of the two joins and the three spaces stand as sent. State now: 79 complete, 36 needs-work, 0 errors. Records are at 60ee3fc9 on my branch.

Both snapshots verified and merged (merge fe0f3878, no conflict, only your files changed; pooled values 9 added, none removed or changed; npm run check passes: 277 tests, 274 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped). (1) 8121f9b2: I compared it with 10d8d38d myself for all 115 items (items, mappings, plans, layouts and the resolved text of 2,618 rows): identical. amal-aamal-stvn-2 and item-mrsyh-am-albnyn are now bound to 8121f9b2; my reviews of the two joins and three spaces are unchanged. (2) 48f3ea69 changes only amal-aamal-shbhay-dhh. I read all 19 rows. The cut on r00012 is accepted: ar 0-274 / 274-285 / 285-694 and fa 0-214 / 214-226 / 226-547, kinds recitation, instruction, recitation; both recitation pairs match clause by clause; every code point is kept; no space is inserted. Links: all 16 row ids of every earlier snapshot of the item are still reachable, r00012 as a mapping original; nothing retired or reused. (3) Your question on the doubled direction: I accept the two adjacent Persian instruction rows. I know of no supported representation that shows it once. Each source code point must stay in exactly one output row and a layout row takes one piece per slot, so showing it once means either dropping one occurrence or putting the Persian words back in the ar slot, which is the fault the cut removed. The doubled line is a property of the source; I accepted the same in amal-bqyh-aamal r00029. If the coordinator wants such duplicates shown once, that needs a tool change, not an author change. The item is complete. State: 80 complete, 35 needs-work, 0 errors; all 115 records name a commit that audit-round can reach. Records at b19aa3a1.
